I troll people. I was just thinking an hour ago maybe, there are two types of people in the world:

  1. People easily offended. As greater thinkers than I have put it these should get offended as often as possible so they can eventually quit their whining bullshit (SJWs I'm looking at you) and get a grip of reality.

  2. People who are not easily offended. These guys won't mind a little trolling now and then and might even enjoy it happening (or ignore it if it's aimed at them).

So as you see - it's a win-win situation! Trolling is great for everyone!

I also have a theory about why trolling is so important nowadays, if anyone is interested...
Let me hear your theory, i am very interested.

I'll use Facebook to start things off. Welcome to Facebook where you can only like stuff, you can never dislike them - there is no button for it. If someone posts a picture of a neo-nazi banner and you just happen to be Jewish what are your options there? Pretty much "like it" or "shut the fuck up". Of course, you could comment something to the effect of "I don't like this" but if you're a Facebook user you'll know that just doesn't happen. But why? Well, the interface isn't designed for that - and design on a site like Facebook (or Voat) speaks volumes. The design really gives you two choices: like it or shut the fuck up. Commenting is more an extension of liking a post than anything else over there.

And if you do make a negative comment then you're probably taking a bait to start a very unproductive discussion so what's even the point? Once again Facebook isn't designed for constructive meaningful deep discussions. You can't even send a Facebook link to someone and say "hey join in on this, there's a great discussion going on" - you can send someone a person's profile page but if they're not mutual friends I guess you're out of luck too. Why is that so, when everything on the web is a link? Well, it's not by chance I assure you.

Of course there are ways around this like mentioning someone in a post or using message groups but these are workarounds - there is no way around the fact that Facebook isn't designed for proper discussion and it wouldn't be too far a stretch to say it's designed against it. It's a platform for shallow entertainment and keeping in touch with friends, not to talk collectively about important stuff.

So why is Facebook by far the largest social platform of choice for most people? Because it fits their world view perfectly. People don't want to be "disliked", they don't want to see talking and thinking that defy their worldviews, they like the way things are and want to keep things that way - safe. People feel very strongly about this and will go to great lengths to hide form the anxiety that this kind of thing gives them. This is why so many people use Facebook for hours every single day - to be entertained (literally "to be kept occupied") http://www.etymonline.com/index.php?term=entertain

This Facebook design is also seen in the culture of civilized countries as "political correctness". From a young age you are taught you absolutely can't hurt people's feelings. It's better to shut up than to risk the chance of offending someone, even if they're wrong. In corporate and military culture is absolutely the same thing - if you start openly criticizing or doubting your superior's choices you're gonna get fired or arrested pretty fast! Or at least get put into a position where you won't matter to anyone anymore and have no chance of evolving your career any further.

The status quo (things as they are) is a very powerful force and if you try to change things you're gonna get fought back, ridiculed or even worse but the fact is we are in dire need of some talking as a species. Our main source of energy (oil) is gonna run out in a few decades, almost half the world population lives under the poverty line (having 1 US dollar per day to spend), the rich folk are laughing all the way to the bank, almost every government is corrupt, millions are dying in senseless wars... Has there ever been a time when we have needed more to sit and talk, as a society? But what do we do instead? Shopping, video-games, NetFlix and Facebook. All day, everyday. Keep me busy, I don't want to think.

So here is where trolling comes in. You can make people see how absurd things are and still have a laugh out of it. You can critique people and ideas with a smile on your face and bring some positive light into this dull world. Sure people will be screaming at you "that's negative/offensive/triggers me" but fuck that - the only negative ones are those that are telling you to shut the fuck up and "just accept things for what they are"! People think they have a right to be who they are, even if they are useless dumb fucks. Well guess what, they do but then again you also have the right to say it right to their faces (free-speech)!

Most people think of trolling as being mean and stalking people online. Please. Here are a few examples of trolling that I think are pretty enlightened, educated and lmao so fucking funny:

  • http://gawker.com/5973890/trolls-launch-twitter-campaign-aimed-at-getting-justin-bieber-fans-to-cut-themselves-nsfw
  • http://notyourgoodfatty.com/the-reddit-bangate-aka-the-fattening/
  • https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LulzSec
  • http://www.419eater.com/
  • https://youtu.be/OknU4GLHJD0

Sure, many people would tell you all of these links (and believe this is just a select few) are all about being childish and destructive but honestly if you can't easily see a political, ethical or security/privacy issue being "discussed" (trolled) in each of them then you're stupid.

So concluding: you may not be able to dislike a post on Facebook but you sure as hell can troll the fuck out of anyone and everyone as much as you like - just remember to keep it entertaining. Some people may get angry and shout back at you. Others will not say anything - but they sure will be listening to what you have to say. And you know what? The world's better off for it. The silence is killing our potential to make this a better place.
